BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL PASO                             )
 ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF ITS RETAIL                             ) Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 ELECTRIC RATES PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE                                )
 NO. 317                                                                 )

              ORDER APPOINTING SUBSTITUTE CO-HEARING EXAMINER

         THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) upon its own motion.

         The Commission appoints Keven Gedko as substitute Co-Hearing Examiner, to replace

Hearing Examiner Jocelyn Barrett, and to preside over this matter with Hearing Examiner Nicholas

Rossi.

                                          BACKGROUND 1

         1.     On March 27, 2026, EPE filed its original Application with the Commission.

         2.     On April 2, 2026, the Commission issued its Order Appointing Co-Hearing

Examiners and Amending Case Caption, in which the Commission appointed Jocelyn Barrett and

Elizabeth Hurst to preside over the matter.2

         3.     On July 20, 2026, the Commission appointed Nicholas Rossi as substitute Co-

Hearing Examiner to replace Elizabeth Hurst, and to preside over the matter with Hearing

Examiner Jocelyn Barrett.3

         4.     On August 6, 2026, EPE filed its Amended Application for Revision of Retail

Electric Rates (“Amended Application”). Specifically, among other assertions, EPE’s Amended

Application states its cost of service demonstrates a $70.7 million non-fuel base rate revenue



1 This order summarizes relevant background. The full electronic record of this proceeding is available at

https://e360.prc.nm.gov/portal/public/#/public/nm-prc/en/home.
2 Order Appointing Co-Hearing Examiners and Amending Case Caption at 3.
3 Order Appointing Substitute Co-Hearing Examiner at 2.
 deficiency, reflecting a 50.5 percent non-fuel base rate increase.4 After deducting other operating

revenues for miscellaneous service charges, EPE requests a net revenue increase of $70.5 million

and a weighted average cost of capital of 8.35 percent.5 Throughout the proceedings, EPE states it

intends to demonstrate that:

                a. its currently authorized rates are no longer just and reasonable, will
                   not adequately attract and encourage investment of capital if left
                   unchanged, and do not allow for reasonable return on investment in
                   public utility plant(s) and property;

                b. its rates and authorized revenues as presently allocated do not
                   adequately reflect the cost of service for the respective classes of
                   electric customers; and

                c. the proposed rates are just and reasonable and should be approved.6

                               FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS

         The Commission finds and concludes:

         5.     The Commission may appoint hearing examiners to preside over this matter.7

         6.     It is necessary to appoint a substitute Co-Hearing Examiner in this matter due to

personnel reassignment in the Commission’s Office of Hearing Examiners.

         7.     The appointment of Keven Gedko as Co-Hearing Examiner in this matter will

provide for administrative efficiency and assist in the orderly and timely resolution of this matter.

         IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

         A.     Co-Hearing Examiner Keven Gedko is hereby appointed to substitute for and

replace Co-Hearing Examiner Jocelyn Barrett, and to preside over this matter with Co-Hearing

Examiner Nicholas Rossi, to take all action necessary and convenient within the limits of the


4 Amended Application at 3.
5 Id.
6 Id. at 8-9.
7 See NMSA 1978, § 62-19-20 (2020); 1.2.2.29 NMAC.

 Hearing Examiners’ authority, conduct any necessary hearings, and take any other action in this

case that is consistent with law, including issuing a recommended decision.

       B.       Hearing Examiner Jocelyn Barrett is hereby removed from this matter.

       C.       This Order is effective when signed.

       D.       In computing time in accordance with statute, regulation, or Commission order, the

computation shall begin on the date that this Order is filed with the Chief Clerk of the

Commission’s Records Management Bureau or the Chief Clerk’s designee.

       SIGNED under the Seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, this 19th day of

August, 2026.

                         NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
